doc: Credentials the ENGINE itself consumes on the session lifecycle, independent of any skill.

Domains were per-SKILL; credentials are per-SUBSYSTEM. LINEAR_API_KEY sat in intake's manifest while session.sh resolves it in-process on EVERY session, so `engine env doctor --domain design` silently skipped a credential every session depends on. These belong to no skill, so they live beside the scripts that read them rather than under skills/.

Consumers — LINEAR_API_KEY: session.sh (SRC_RELATED_TICKETS, every activate), engine.sh, linear-lib.sh, project.sh, ticket-search.sh. GEMINI_API_KEY: session.sh (RAG at activate), gemini.sh, research.sh, rewrite.sh, doc-search.sh, session-search.sh.

⚠️ MEMBERSHIP TEST, and it is not 'shared by several things'. A core row must (a) have a consumer on the SESSION LIFECYCLE, not just several skills, and (b) be fail-soft. SLACK_INTAKE_TOKEN fails both: its only consumers are slack-lib/slack-post/slack-read, which exist to serve /intake's announce, and it is `req` — composing a `req` row into every domain hard-blocks a design operator on a Slack app they will never create, which is the exact anti-pattern per-domain manifests exist to prevent. It stays in intake.

The DOCTOR composes core + the named domain, so every domain is checked against these. `env_load_domain` deliberately does NOT — sweeping engine credentials into every /prove publish would be a credential-surface widening nobody asked for.

credentials.how: Linear API key for GraphQL READS — `engine ticket-search`, `engine project`, and the related-ticket lookup at session startup. SHARED, not per-person, and that is safe for a specific reason: these paths issue zero mutations (checked), and a read carries no attribution, so a per-person copy would buy nothing. Every Linear WRITE — comments, issues, status updates — goes through the per-person `linear` MCP and is untouched by this. Fetched from Secrets Manager; never typed. ⚠️ The stored key is presently a personal one promoted to shared: it works, and it dies when that person leaves. Re-point it at a service account before anything depends on it.

Gemini API key, MINTED PER PERSON by `engine env provision` on the Finch Google project and stored in Secrets Manager — you never obtain one yourself and never type it. Per-person because that is what buys ATTRIBUTION (whose agent spent it) and REVOCATION (kill one key without rotating everyone). ⚠️ It does NOT buy a per-person spend cap: Gemini quota and billing are per PROJECT, so the ceiling is shared and one runaway still stops everyone — the keys tell you who, not how much. Restricted to generativelanguage.googleapis.com only, so a leaked key reaches nothing else on the project. Powers `engine gemini`, `engine research`, `engine rewrite` and the doc-search / session-search RAG at session activate; all fail soft without it.

Google Cloud project the per-person Gemini keys are minted on. DELIBERATELY SEPARATE from the product's own Gemini project: quota and billing are per PROJECT, so agent keys living beside the app's would let a runaway agent throttle the product. This project holds agent keys and nothing else, which is where the isolation that matters actually lands — agents share a ceiling with each other (they are peers) and share nothing with the app. `engine env provision` creates a key here restricted to generativelanguage.googleapis.com and stores it at staging/finch/gemini-key/<person>. Declared as a manifest row so re-pointing the whole fleet is a default change rather than a code edit — which is exactly what happened the first time.
